subject: Syncly POC — pricing vs latency priorities and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana@syncly.ai>, Chris Park <chris@syncly.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Syncly POC — pricing vs latency priorities and next steps

Hi Dana / Chris —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and a few concrete asks so we can get the POC scoped and pricing aligned to your goals. I summarized the options we discussed for latency vs cost and noted the follow-ups we need to finalize a binding estimate.

Summary of discovery points
- Primary workload: user-facing chat for customer support + async summarization for transcripts.
- Peak concurrency estimate you gave: ~120 simultaneous sessions during daytime peaks; median session length ~3 minutes, average tokens/session ~900.
- Target latency for chat: 95th pctile under 250ms preferred; acceptable up to 500ms if costs become prohibitive.
- Budget band you mentioned: $6k–$12k/mo for inference (initial POC).

Options we proposed (high level unit economics)
- Low-latency streaming tier (hosted, streaming outputs): approx $600 per 1M tokens (optimized for 95th pctile latency <250ms); recommended for chat-first user experience.
- Cost-optimized batch tier (hosted or dedicated): approx $220 per 1M tokens (higher throughput, increased token batching; 95th pctile latency typically 500–1200ms depending on batch settings).
- Hybrid routing (production): route interactive queries to streaming tier and background/summary jobs to batch; blended unit ~$310–$380 per 1M tokens depending on traffic split and caching.

Key trade-offs to confirm
1) Is 95th pctile <250ms a hard SLO for the POC or a target?
2) Can you confirm expected tokens/day (or tokens/month) for the POC window so we can give a per-month estimate?
3) Are you open to an initial hosted POC with dedicated capacity for peak windows, or do you need a full dedicated commit?

Next steps (mutual action plan)
- Syncly: share a 24–72h sample traffic export (or histogram of token/session and concurrency) — action: Dana (by EOD Thu).
- Redwood: produce a two-line pricing workbook (streaming vs batch vs hybrid) and a PO-friendly SOW for the POC + a one-page operations checklist — action: Alex (by Wed).
- Redwood SEs: recommend batching/window settings for background jobs and an initial routing policy — action: Lauren & Grace (by Wed).

Attachments: I attached the POC requirements doc you sent and our initial pricing matrix (stubs below).
Attachments (stubs): syncly_poc_requirements.pdf (pdf), redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

If the 95th-pctile <250ms is critical, we should assume the streaming tier for chat and size accordingly. If it's a preference but not required, hybrid routing is likely the most economical for your stated budget band.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai

> - Streaming tier: will need ~3–4 streaming GPU slots to hold 250ms 95th with small batch windows.
> - Batch tier: 2–3 GPUs with aggressive batching can hit lower unit cost but will add latency.
>
> I'll draft recommended batch-window values for background jobs and a fallback policy (route to batch if queue depth > X).
>

From: Dana Liu <dana@syncly.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Park <chris@syncly.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 17:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Syncly POC — pricing vs latency priorities and next steps

Alex —

Appreciate the clear recap. Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) 95th <250ms would be ideal for chat; however, we can accept up to 350ms during spikes for the POC if it significantly reduces costs.
2) Our procurement lead needs a firm not-to-exceed monthly estimate to get internal approval for the POC — can you provide a conservative hosted estimate and a separate dedicated-reserved estimate?

We can get you a 72-hour sample and the token histograms by Thursday EOD — will include daytime and overnight windows.

Also: question on caching — do you support prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts across sessions to reduce tokens billed? If so, can you note expected savings range?

Thanks,
Dana Liu
Head of Product, Syncly
dana@syncly.ai

On Tue, Dec 22, 2026 at 5:02 PM Chris Park <chris@syncly.ai> wrote:
> Adding procurement on the note; procurement@syncly.ai will need PO language and an estimated monthly cap.
> — Chris
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Syncly POC — pricing vs latency priorities and next steps

Alex / Grace —

I sketched conservative sizing and savings assumptions while they prep the sample traffic:
- Conservative hosted estimate (streaming-only chat): assume 1.2M tokens/day => ~36M tokens/month => $21.6k/mo at $600 per 1M (streaming).
- Conservative hosted estimate (hybrid: 60% streaming / 40% batch): blended unit ~ $396/1M => ~ $14.3k/mo.
- Dedicated reserved (monthly commit + reserved discount): ballpark 20–30% off hosted list => $10k–$11.4k/mo for the hybrid case depending on commit and burst policy.

Caching note: prefix/KV caching typically reduces billed tokens for high-reuse prompts by 10–40% depending on reuse patterns. For chat-support where templates and KB snippets repeat, expect mid-case ~20% token savings. We'll mark assumptions in the workbook.

I'll attach the two-line workbook and an initial SOW draft once Alex creates the cover email.

— Lauren
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Syncly POC — pricing vs latency priorities and next steps

Dana / Procurement team —

Thanks — attaching the conservative pricing workbook and a short POC SOW (attached as stubs here for the thread). High-level conservative estimates below for your procurement review (not-to-exceed numbers for POC):

Conservative hosted (streaming-only)
- Assumption: 36M tokens/month
- Unit: $600 / 1M tokens
- Monthly estimate: $21,600 (not-to-exceed for hosted POC)

Conservative hosted (hybrid, 60/40 split streaming/batch)
- Blended unit: $396 / 1M tokens
- Monthly estimate: $14,256 (not-to-exceed for hosted hybrid POC)

Dedicated reserved (12-month commit ballpark)
- Estimated blended after reserve discount: $10,000–$11,400 / mo (depends on commit level & burst capacity)

SLO note: if Syncly requires 95th <250ms for chat, we'll size the streaming footprint and provide an SLA appendix in the SOW; if 350ms is acceptable during spikes, hybrid routing will materially reduce costs.

Caching savings: we assumed 20% token savings in the hybrid workbook (call out: range 10–40% depending on reuse).

Requested from Syncly
- 72-hour sample or histogram (tokens/session, concurrency) — Dana (EOD Thu)
- Procurement timeline / PO owner + PO template — procurement@syncly.ai

Redwood deliverables (this week)
- Two-line pricing workbook (attached): redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx — Alex
- POC SOW and operations checklist: syncly_poc_sow_draft.pdf — Alex
- Routing & batching playbook: Lauren & Grace

If procurement needs a single not-to-exceed line for approval, recommend we propose the hosted hybrid estimate ($14,256) and note the dedicated range as an alternative if they want predictable unit economics. Happy to jump on a brief call with procurement to walk through the SOW.

Best,
Alex Martinez
